clock_get_time: Rejects a null clock, then calls that clock’s `c_gettime` operation. The system-clock implementation converts system nanoseconds into `mach_timespec_t`; the calendar implementation uses calendar nanoseconds instead. The destination clock object selects the time domain, rather than a caller-supplied flavor. [clock_get_time](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/clock_oldops.c#L274-L310).
clock_get_attributes: Requires a clock object and an installed `c_getattr` callback. The supplied clocks require exactly one output word. System-clock resolution and alarm-resolution flavors return a 10 ms value; the calendar clock reports the same time resolution but zero alarm resolution. Unknown flavors return `KERN_INVALID_VALUE`; a missing operation returns `KERN_FAILURE`. [clock_get_attributes](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/clock_oldops.c#L316-L380).
host_get_clock_service: Checks the host and bounds of the clock ID, selects the static `clock_list` entry, and rejects an entry lacking operations. The output is the clock service object converted by MIG into its capability; this operation neither allocates a new clock nor grants a clock-control implementation. [host_get_clock_service](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/clock_oldops.c#L253-L268).
clock_alarm: Only the system clock is supported. A missing reply capability fails immediately; an invalid or already-due time instead produces an immediate alarm reply and returns RPC success. Future alarms take a recycled or newly allocated record under the alarm lock, store the reply right, deadline and sequence number, then enter the ordered alarm machinery. Allocation drops and reacquires the lock. [clock_alarm](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/clock_oldops.c#L388-L452).
semaphore_create: Validates the task, nonnegative initial value and user policy mask before allocating a zeroed semaphore. Under the task lock it rechecks task activity, initializes a locked wait queue and reference count, and links the semaphore into the owner’s list. A termination race frees the new object and returns `KERN_INVALID_TASK`; success publishes the initialized semaphore after releasing both locks. [semaphore_create](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L94-L145).
semaphore_destroy: Consumes the supplied semaphore reference even when the task argument is invalid. If the task owns the semaphore, it rechecks ownership under the task lock, unlinks the object, clears its owner/count under the semaphore lock, and wakes waiters with `THREAD_RESTART`. A valid non-owner task does not destroy the semaphore but still returns success after dropping the reference; waiters translate destruction into `KERN_TERMINATED`. [semaphore_destroy](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L158-L194). [Ownership check and reference consumption](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L285-L311).
semaphore_signal: Takes the semaphore lock at scheduler interrupt level and rejects an inactive object. It wakes one queued waiter when possible; otherwise the PREPOST option increments the available count. The public wrapper converts the internal `KERN_NOT_WAITING` result into success, so callers cannot distinguish a wakeup from a stored permit through the return value. [semaphore_signal](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L338-L415). [Public result conversion](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L495-L515).
semaphore_signal_all: Uses the shared signal helper with ALL but without PREPOST. When waiters exist, it sets the count to zero and wakes every waiter while releasing the wait-queue lock and restoring interrupt state. With a nonnegative count, it leaves that count unchanged: the implementation is narrower than the nearby comment that says the count always returns to zero. Inactive semaphores fail with `KERN_TERMINATED`. [semaphore_signal_all](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L338-L388).
semaphore_signal_thread: A non-null thread restricts the wakeup to that thread on this semaphore’s wait queue; absence of that waiter returns `KERN_NOT_WAITING`. A null thread selects any existing waiter. Unlike ordinary signal, this call does not prepost a permit when nobody is waiting. The semaphore lock and scheduler interrupt level protect the active/count check and wakeup selection. [semaphore_signal_thread](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L338-L415).
semaphore_wait: Under the semaphore lock, consumes an available permit or records the presence of waiters with count `-1` and asserts an abort-safe wait. The count is a waiter-present marker, not a negative waiter total. After unlocking, the non-continuation MIG body blocks through the handoff helper and translates wakeup, timeout, interruption and destruction into success, timed-out, aborted and terminated results. [semaphore_wait](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L605-L623). [Wait registration and blocking](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L659-L801).
semaphore_timedwait: Rejects an invalid timespec before touching the wait queue. `{0,0}` selects a nonblocking attempt; a positive interval becomes an absolute deadline. The shared locked wait path first consumes an existing permit, so a zero timeout can succeed; otherwise it returns timed-out or installs an abort-safe timed wait. The MIG wrapper uses the stack-preserving, non-continuation form. [semaphore_timedwait](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L867-L892).
semaphore_wait_signal: Registers the wait, or resolves an immediately available permit/error, before signaling the second semaphore. The wait lock is released before the signal lock is acquired. A waiting caller can hand execution directly to the awakened signal waiter. If the signal semaphore has died, it clears its own wait; an already-delivered wakeup wins, otherwise interruption is converted to `KERN_TERMINATED`. [semaphore_wait_signal](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L659-L778).
semaphore_timedwait_signal: Validates the wait timespec, selects a nonblocking attempt for zero or computes an absolute deadline, then uses the same wait-before-signal protocol. Even when waiting resolves immediately, the helper still signals the second semaphore before returning. Invalid timespecs are rejected before that side effect. Signal-semaphore destruction explicitly cancels the pending wait rather than leaving the caller stranded. [semaphore_timedwait_signal](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L1020-L1047). [Signal and cancellation ordering](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sync_sema.c#L704-L752).
task_restartable_ranges_register: Only the current task may register. Validation precedes the task lock; translated tasks are rejected when Rosetta is configured. Installation requires a single-threaded task, and release kernels also reject replacing an existing registration. The creator installs the validated range representation while task creation is serialized by the task lock; failures leave the old registration intact. [task_restartable_ranges_register](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/restartable.c#L535-L579).
task_restartable_ranges_synchronize: Only the current task is accepted; no registered ranges is a successful no-op. A priority floor bounds scheduler interference while the task lock serializes synchronization, with concurrent callers rejected as already waiting. A release fence precedes posting RESET_PCS ASTs to other threads. The caller waits for required acknowledgments/fault resolution, restarts enumeration after lock-dropping waits, then clears the in-flight flag and releases its priority floor. [task_restartable_ranges_synchronize](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/restartable.c#L583-L685).
processor_start_from_user: The wrapper holds the cluster-powerdown mutex while the scheduler helper checks device support, system-required CPU rules, suspended powerdown, current user-online state and disabled-SMT restrictions. Success sets the user-online bit; restoring all managed CPUs ends manual user core control, and resulting power changes are applied through scheduler machinery. Pulled threads are flushed after scheduler locking is released. [Wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1277-L1293), [scheduler decisions](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sched_prim.c#L7465-L7532).
processor_exit_from_user: Serializes with cluster powerdown, then takes the available-cores lock at scheduler interrupt level. The helper rejects unsupported/system-required CPUs, PMGR constraints, suspended powerdown, an already user-offlined CPU, and removal of the last available core. Success clears the user-online bit and applies any resulting powered-core change; pulled runnable threads are flushed after unlocking. [Wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1222-L1238), [scheduler decisions](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/sched_prim.c#L7390-L7462).
processor_control: After rejecting a null processor, forwards its stable CPU ID and the opaque flavor-dependent word array to the machine `cpu_control` implementation. The generic routine adds no policy changes or scheduling operations; architecture-specific support and its error code determine the result. [processor_control](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1427-L1437).
processor_assign: This implementation ignores the processor, destination set and wait argument and always returns `KERN_FAILURE`. It does not migrate a CPU or wait for a change, despite the historical interface declaration. [processor_assign](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/machine.c#L224-L230).
processor_get_assignment: Reads the processor state and rejects offline or pending-offline processors. For an eligible processor it returns `sched_boot_pset`, rather than exposing that processor’s internal cluster set. Thus the user-visible assignment API presents the compatibility processor set, not the scheduler’s full internal topology. [processor_get_assignment](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1440-L1458).
processor_info: Dispatches basic-info and CPU-load flavors locally after checking output capacity, and passes other flavors to `cpu_info`. Basic-info treats temporary shutdown specially and on x86 also excludes nonrecommended processors. Load output starts with zeroed system/user/idle fields, fills accounted ticks, and explicitly leaves NICE at zero. The host output is set only on a successful flavor implementation. [processor_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L869-L951).
processor_set_default: A non-null host returns `sched_boot_pset`. No set is created and no scheduler state is changed; MIG converts this existing compatibility-set object into the requested processor-set capability. A null host fails before publishing an output object. [processor_set_default](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_host.c#L221-L233).
processor_set_statistics: Only the boot compatibility set is accepted. LOAD_INFO reports global scheduler load/Mach-factor values and global task/thread totals after checking capacity; the routine does not aggregate a private membership list under a set lock. Unsupported flavors return invalid-argument, while another set returns invalid-processor-set. [processor_set_statistics](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1595-L1627).
processor_set_info: Rejects a null set and dispatches compatibility information flavors with per-layout capacity checks. BASIC_INFO reports the global available processor count and timeshare default; policy defaults/limits expose scheduler constants rather than a configurable independent set policy. Successful flavors return the real host and their actual word count; unsupported flavors fail. [processor_set_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1461-L1590).
processor_set_tasks: The shared enumeration accepts only `sched_boot_pset`, allocates arrays outside `tasks_threads_lock`, then retries until capacity covers the current global lists. It references IPC-active, non-exec-copy tasks under the lock, filters them through MAC exposure policy afterward, compacts the result, and converts references into task ports. The flavored entry validates CONTROL/READ/INSPECT/NAME; the older entry selects CONTROL. Allocation and filtering therefore precede capability publication. [processor_set_tasks](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1636-L1922).
processor_set_tasks_with_flavor: The shared enumeration accepts only `sched_boot_pset`, allocates arrays outside `tasks_threads_lock`, then retries until capacity covers the current global lists. It references IPC-active, non-exec-copy tasks under the lock, filters them through MAC exposure policy afterward, compacts the result, and converts references into task ports. The flavored entry validates CONTROL/READ/INSPECT/NAME; the older entry selects CONTROL. Allocation and filtering therefore precede capability publication. [processor_set_tasks_with_flavor](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/processor.c#L1636-L1922).
host_info: Dispatches each host flavor with layout-specific capacity checks, rather than returning one fixed snapshot. BASIC_INFO accepts the older short layout, conditionally reports the extended layout, and adjusts available CPUs for SMT policy. Scheduler info converts the active scheduler’s initial quantum into milliseconds; trap-availability flavors return zero words. Resource-size information remains an explicit invalid-argument branch. [host_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L204-L337).
host_kernel_version: Requires a non-null host, then copies the global kernel version string into the fixed-size `kernel_version_t` result with bounded `strncpy`. It does not allocate an OOL buffer or query a separately running service. [host_kernel_version](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1203-L1213).
host_page_size: Requires a non-null host and returns the kernel’s `PAGE_SIZE`. This is not a query of an arbitrary task map’s page mask or the hardware geometry selected by that map’s pmap. [host_page_size](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1185-L1194).
host_statistics_from_user: The user wrapper validates the host, then invokes the rate-limiter/cache helper before reading statistics. A cached reply or rate-limit error returns immediately. Otherwise it calls the corresponding statistics dispatcher and caches only a successful result. The 64-bit dispatcher handles its extended flavors and can fall back to the ordinary dispatcher; these wrappers therefore have different freshness semantics from direct kernel calls. [host_statistics_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1061-L1111).
host_statistics64_from_user: The user wrapper validates the host, then invokes the rate-limiter/cache helper before reading statistics. A cached reply or rate-limit error returns immediately. Otherwise it calls the corresponding statistics dispatcher and caches only a successful result. The 64-bit dispatcher handles its extended flavors and can fall back to the ordinary dispatcher; these wrappers therefore have different freshness semantics from direct kernel calls. [host_statistics64_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1061-L1111).
host_priv_statistics: Forwards directly to `host_statistics` with the privileged-host object cast to a host. The body adds no privileged statistics flavor and bypasses the separate user statistics wrapper’s rate-limiter/cache path; flavor validation and output sizing belong to the ordinary dispatcher. [host_priv_statistics](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1119-L1122).
host_processor_info: Obtains the per-CPU record size for the requested flavor, allocates a rounded IPC-kernel-map buffer, and fills each slot by calling `processor_info`. A per-CPU failure frees the allocation. Success zeroes trailing page padding, unwires the buffer, and turns the used bytes into a source-destroying VM copy for the OOL reply. Processor count and total word count describe that packed array. [host_processor_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1271-L1335).
host_processors: Requires a privileged-host object and allocates an array sized to the global processor count. Each `processor_array` object is converted to a processor send right before the array is published. Allocation failure returns resource-shortage; this enumerates registered processor objects, rather than filtering to currently running CPUs. [host_processors](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L171-L199).
host_processor_sets: Allocates exactly one port-array element and returns a name capability for `sched_boot_pset`. Internal cluster processor sets are not enumerated through this compatibility interface. Null host is rejected; allocation uses the waiting, no-fail path. [host_processor_sets](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1220-L1243).
host_processor_set_priv: Requires both a privileged host and an existing processor-set-name object. It returns that same set object for control-port conversion, rather than allocating another set or modifying membership. Invalid arguments explicitly clear the output set before returning failure. [host_processor_set_priv](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1250-L1262).
host_get_io_main: Rejects a null ordinary host, then obtains the IO main special port through the privileged-host helper using the kernel’s real host object. The returned right names the existing IOKit service endpoint; no driver or registry object is instantiated by this call. [host_get_io_main](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1516-L1523).
kmod_get_info: This body only logs that the operation is unsupported on the kernel architecture, including the caller’s process name, and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. It does not enumerate OSKext objects despite the retained OOL result declaration. [kmod_get_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/kmod.c#L98-L105).
host_virtual_physical_table_info: The local routine unconditionally returns `KERN_FAILURE`; it does not fill the historical physical-hash-bucket array. The retained interface should not be used as evidence of a supported pmap introspection mechanism. [host_virtual_physical_table_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/vm/vm_debug.c#L152-L158).
host_request_notification: Validates the host, send-once reply capability and notification selector, then allocates a host-notify record. Under the global notify lock and port queue lock it registers a port request and queues the record; successful registration also makes an ordinary in-space receive right immovable. A full request table is grown after dropping locks and retried; other errors free the record without installing it. [host_request_notification](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host_notify.c#L65-L130).
host_lockgroup_info: Allocates a zeroed IPC-map buffer with modest growth slack, then enumerates lock groups and copies counters/names until capacity is reached. DTrace counters are configuration-dependent and the fields are not a globally atomic snapshot. Unused trailing pages are freed; the used pages are unwired and converted to a source-destroying VM copy for the OOL result. [host_lockgroup_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/lock_group.c#L331-L410).
host_set_atm_diagnostic_flag: Requires a valid host and the private set-atm-diagnostic-flag entitlement. With ATM configured it delegates to `atm_set_diagnostic_config`; otherwise it returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED` after those admission checks. Possession of the ordinary host port alone is insufficient to change the setting. [host_set_atm_diagnostic_flag](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1538-L1553).
host_set_multiuser_config_flags: On non-macOS targets, validates the privileged-host object and directly updates the commpage multiuser configuration. On macOS the body ignores both arguments and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. This call updates the published bit configuration, not a set of user accounts or per-process credentials. [host_set_multiuser_config_flags](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1557-L1576).
mach_zone_info: Delegates to `mach_memory_info` without requesting the auxiliary memory-information array. That entry first attempts privileged-host conversion; ordinary-host conversion selects redacted output. The shared implementation applies memory-information security checks and packages zone names/statistics into OOL VM copies, so this older call inherits redaction, coalescing and admission behavior. [mach_zone_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8194-L8224).
mach_memory_info: Uses the raw destination port to distinguish a privileged host from an ordinary host, selecting redaction for the latter. Shared sampling performs root/entitlement/rate-limit checks as configured. Redacted samples zero sensitive size fields and coalesce typed-allocation zones by element size; full samples also accumulate collectable bytes. Results are returned as VM-copy arrays, not pointers into live zone metadata. [mach_memory_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8100-L8144). [Port conversion and sampling](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8205-L8370).
mach_memory_info_redacted: Forces redaction even when a more powerful destination capability was supplied, converting it through the host interface. The common security check permits non-root redacted requests but can still require the memory-information entitlement. Sampling removes sensitive size information and combines same-sized typed-zone statistics before producing independent OOL output arrays. [mach_memory_info_redacted](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8227-L8370).
mach_zone_force_gc: Validates the host. Only DEBUG/DEVELOPMENT builds call the optional buffer-cache collector followed by `zone_gc(ZONE_GC_DRAIN)`; other builds return success without performing that collection. A successful return therefore does not universally demonstrate that any zone pages were reclaimed. [mach_zone_force_gc](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8722-L8739).
mach_zone_info_for_zone: Requires a valid host and output pointer, with an additional debugger-availability gate in protected zone-info configurations. It builds each zone’s heap-prefixed name and uses `track_this_zone` to find a match, then snapshots that zone through `get_zone_info`. Missing names return invalid-argument; a failed snapshot returns failure. [mach_zone_info_for_zone](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8505-L8551).
mach_zone_info_for_largest_zone: Applies the host/debugger gate and validates both output pointers, then asks `zone_find_largest` for the current largest zone and snapshots its name/statistics with `get_zone_info`. It does not reclaim that zone or pin its population against later changes. Snapshot failure is reported as `KERN_FAILURE`. [mach_zone_info_for_largest_zone](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8554-L8577).
mach_zone_get_zlog_zones: When zone logging is compiled in, validates the host and outputs, allocates a pageable IPC-map name buffer sized to the current zone count, and includes only zones with a `z_btlog`. The used names become a VM-copy result. Without `ZALLOC_ENABLE_LOGGING`, the routine simply returns `KERN_FAILURE`. [mach_zone_get_zlog_zones](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8596-L8649).
mach_zone_get_btlog_records: With zone logging enabled, finds the heap-prefixed zone name, rejects an absent zone or missing log, then obtains a record snapshot from `btlog_get_records`. It converts that allocated snapshot into a source-destroying VM copy for reply ownership. Allocation/helper errors propagate; a build without logging returns failure rather than an empty successful snapshot. [mach_zone_get_btlog_records](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/zalloc.c#L8652-L8717).
mach_memory_object_memory_entry: The common 64-bit implementation validates host, size and permissions, then either allocates an internal VM object when no pager was supplied or references the VM object represented by the pager. It creates a named entry, stores size/protection/access, associates the object range, and records internal/ownership attributes. A missing backing object is invalid-argument. The older-sized routine only forwards into this implementation. [mach_memory_object_memory_entry](../../../xnu/osfmk/vm/vm_memory_entry.c#L1340-L1405).
mach_memory_object_memory_entry_64: The common 64-bit implementation validates host, size and permissions, then either allocates an internal VM object when no pager was supplied or references the VM object represented by the pager. It creates a named entry, stores size/protection/access, associates the object range, and records internal/ownership attributes. A missing backing object is invalid-argument. The older-sized routine only forwards into this implementation. [mach_memory_object_memory_entry_64](../../../xnu/osfmk/vm/vm_memory_entry.c#L1340-L1405).
host_get_boot_info: Requires a privileged-host object, then asks the machine boot-info helper to fill or return a string. If the helper returned a different buffer, the wrapper copies it into the bounded output array. The machine backend determines the actual boot-information contents; this is not a direct export of all firmware or device-tree state. [host_get_boot_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/machine.c#L587-L607).
host_reboot: Rejects a null privileged host. Development/debug builds honor the debugger option by entering `Debugger` and returning. The UPS-delay option calls the platform halt/restart hook; other requests call `halt_all_cpus`, with the HALT bit selecting halt versus restart. The RPC is therefore a thin privileged entry into machine/platform shutdown, not a BSD filesystem-sync transaction. [host_reboot](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/machine.c#L198-L221).
host_default_memory_manager: Serializes access with `memory_manager_default_lock`. A null incoming manager queries the current manager by making a send right. Replacement is restricted to the kernel task even with a privileged host, starts internal pager support for the first manager, and on success returns the old reference while making a send right for the new stored manager. Startup errors leave the stored manager unchanged. [host_default_memory_manager](../../../xnu/osfmk/vm/memory_object.c#L1413-L1485).
vm_wire: The common implementation requires a privileged host and target map, computes the unsafe end address for the sanitizing map helpers, and interprets zero protection as unwire. Nonzero protection requests user-accounted wiring with the MLOCK tag; zero requests user unwiring. Validation, range walking and partial-work cleanup belong to `vm_map_wire_impl`/`vm_map_unwire_impl`; the older-sized entry simply forwards. [vm_wire](../../../xnu/osfmk/vm/vm_user.c#L1127-L1175).
mach_vm_wire_external: The common implementation requires a privileged host and target map, computes the unsafe end address for the sanitizing map helpers, and interprets zero protection as unwire. Nonzero protection requests user-accounted wiring with the MLOCK tag; zero requests user unwiring. Validation, range walking and partial-work cleanup belong to `vm_map_wire_impl`/`vm_map_unwire_impl`; the older-sized entry simply forwards. [mach_vm_wire_external](../../../xnu/osfmk/vm/vm_user.c#L1127-L1175).
thread_wire: The current body ignores every argument and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. It does not set the thread’s VM-privilege option; the separately implemented kernel privilege helpers nearby are not the behavior of this MIG operation. [thread_wire](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L2310-L2316).
host_set_special_port_from_user: Rejects kernel-owned slots, DriverKit callers, and send rights that cannot safely be stashed. The downstream setter permits kernel/init callers or the applicable entitlement/CSR exception, applies MAC policy, then swaps the host slot under its lock. The old send right is released afterward. Success transfers ownership of the new right to the host slot. [host_set_special_port_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1347-L1451).
host_get_special_port_from_user: Rejects invalid IDs and the security port. Driver tasks cannot obtain user-owned special ports except the entitled HID sysdiagnose exception. Under the host lock, the helper clones the appropriate right: host kobjects use typed copies, IO main uses its dedicated endpoint, and other slots use mqueue send-right copying. The node argument is ignored locally. [host_get_special_port_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/host.c#L1461-L1507).
host_set_exception_ports: Validates mask/behavior/flavor and MAC permission before taking the host lock. Selected exception actions receive copies of the new right and updated behavior/flavor, subject to per-action label updates. Lazy MAC labels are prepared outside the lock; displaced rights and unused labels are released afterward. Success consumes the supplied send right, rather than storing that one reference in every action. [host_set_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_host.c#L492-L588).
host_get_exception_ports: Under the host lock, groups selected exception actions with identical port, behavior and state flavor into one result mask. Each newly represented group gets a copied send right, up to the caller’s supplied capacity. The output count is the groups actually returned; this query does not clear registrations or transfer their stored rights. [host_get_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_host.c#L606-L657).
host_swap_exception_ports: After validating the replacement and MAC permission, snapshots grouped old actions while installing copied replacement rights under the host lock. The loop is bounded by the supplied output capacity, so insufficient capacity limits which later exception types are processed rather than merely truncating a separately completed full swap. Old stored rights and the supplied replacement right are released after unlocking. [host_swap_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_host.c#L660-L780).
host_set_UNDServer: With user notifications configured, this is a wrapper around the host user-notification special-port helper, so its authorization and right ownership follow the host special-port operation. Without `CONFIG_USER_NOTIFICATION` it ignores the arguments and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; the interface declaration does not guarantee a notification-daemon backend. [host_set_UNDServer](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L364-L376).
host_get_UNDServer: With user notifications configured, this is a wrapper around the host user-notification special-port helper, so its authorization and right ownership follow the host special-port operation. Without `CONFIG_USER_NOTIFICATION` it ignores the arguments and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; the interface declaration does not guarantee a notification-daemon backend. [host_get_UNDServer](../../../xnu/osfmk/UserNotification/KUNCUserNotifications.c#L381-L391).
host_create_mach_voucher: Validates the host then invokes the common voucher creator without an attribute-control capability and with user-data recipe conversion enabled. The creator allocates an initially empty voucher, walks bounded recipes, resolves previous-voucher names, applies attribute-manager commands, and releases partially built state on failure. Successful construction deduplicates the voucher’s attribute set before publishing a reference. [host_create_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/ipc/ipc_voucher.c#L1407-L1559).
kext_request: Clears all reply outputs before consuming the incoming VM-copy request into kernel-map memory. It distinguishes mkext binary loading from XML requests: secure/no-KXLD builds reject mkext, and loading requires the privileged host. OSKext operations report a separate `op_result`; response/log buffers become OOL copies. Copyout failure leaves input-copy cleanup to MIG, whereas a successfully mapped input is deallocated by the finish path. [kext_request](../../../xnu/libkern/OSKextLib.cpp#L218-L394).
task_terminate: The public body rejects a null task and refuses any task with BSD process information, so it is not the ordinary process-exit entry. The accepted Mach-only path serializes task state, holds threads, marks the task inactive and disables task IPC before requesting thread termination. It subsequently destroys owned synchronizers, terminates the IPC space and VM map, and moves the task to the terminated-task list; storage remains reference-counted. [Public admission](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L2445-L2457), [ordered termination](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L2982-L3210).
task_threads_from_user: Converts the destination to an inspectable task without the usual conversion evaluation, then uses its actual CONTROL/READ/INSPECT kobject type to choose the corresponding thread-port flavor. The helper retries allocation outside the task lock, references the active task’s threads under that lock, and converts them into ports afterward. Failed resizing drops all collected references; the wrapper always drops its temporary task reference. [task_threads_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L3852-L3985).
_kernelrpc_mach_ports_register3: Checks all three incoming rights for stashability before taking the task IPC lock. If IPC is inactive it fails without replacing slots. Otherwise it exchanges the complete registered-port array while locked and releases the displaced send rights after unlocking. Success transfers the supplied rights into inheritable task slots; no OOL array allocation occurs in this three-port server form. [_kernelrpc_mach_ports_register3](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L2184-L2235).
_kernelrpc_mach_ports_lookup3: Under the task IPC lock, rejects an inactive task and clones each of its three registered send rights into separate outputs. Stored references remain in the task; the caller receives additional rights. This fixed-arity server form avoids the older client API’s apparent variable-length array contract, which is handled outside this body. [_kernelrpc_mach_ports_lookup3](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L2251-L2275).
task_info_from_user: Chooses the capability conversion by information flavor: DYLD_INFO requires task-read access, while other flavors use task-name conversion. The common dispatcher locks the task, rejects an inactive foreign task, checks the requested layout count, and collects flavor-specific map, ledger, accounting or policy data. The wrapper drops its converted task reference on every return; passing a null conversion through the dispatcher yields invalid-argument. [task_info_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L5291-L5330). [Flavor-dependent conversion](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L6417-L6437).
task_set_info: After checking that the task is non-null, this dispatcher supports no mutable information flavor. With ATM configured, TASK_TRACE_MEMORY_INFO explicitly returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; all other flavors return `KERN_INVALID_ARGUMENT`. It neither copies an arbitrary information block into the task nor changes the data returned by task_info. [task_set_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L5251-L5269).
task_suspend: Places a legacy hold under the task lock, rejecting null/kernel targets and failing for a dead noncorpse task. The first user hold suspends constituent threads and waits for user execution to stop. It then makes a send right to the task resume kobject and copies that hidden token into the caller’s IPC space; abandoning rights enables no-senders cleanup. Copyout errors are reported after the hold was placed. [task_suspend](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L3987-L4071). [Legacy token publication](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L4141-L4197).
task_resume: Releases a legacy hold under the task lock, then searches the caller’s IPC space for the task’s resume-port token. It deallocates one right after a successful release or destroys the found entry when release failed. Missing tokens do not undo an otherwise successful resume; they only trigger an out-of-band warning. Final hold release is what resumes constituent threads. [task_resume](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L4207-L4259).
task_suspend2_mig: Calls the normal task-hold path, then acquires a TASK_GRP_MIG reference and returns the task as a suspension-token object. MIG converts that reference into the token capability. Each successful call represents its own normal hold; a failed suspension clears the output token. It shares task/null/kernel/activity checks and first-hold thread waiting with the common hold machinery. [task_suspend2_mig](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L4266-L4309).
task_resume2_mig: Uses the supplied suspension token to release a normal task hold under the task lock, then unconditionally deallocates the token’s grouped task reference. The cleanup occurs even if resuming fails. Null/kernel targets and missing eligible holds fail through the common resume path; the final successful hold release wakes the task’s threads. [task_resume2_mig](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L4324-L4360).
task_get_special_port_from_user: Converts the incoming task capability to an inspectable object, applies MAC policy, and separately checks requests for a movable self-control port. It preserves the destination’s CONTROL/READ/INSPECT strength when calling the internal selector: read access can obtain read/inspect/name, while inspect permits inspect/name only. The temporary task reference is released regardless of selector or policy failure. [task_get_special_port_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L1887-L1985).
task_set_special_port_from_user: Applies MAC policy before the kernel setter’s DriverKit, stashability and CSR checks. The internal operation takes the task IPC lock, requires an existing control-port object, and swaps only supported slots; TASK_ACCESS_PORT cannot be overwritten once valid. Unlike an IPC-active check, the control-port existence check permits spawn-time setup before task IPC publication. Displaced send rights are released after unlocking. [task_set_special_port_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L2004-L2161).
task_set_exception_ports: Validates exception semantics and MAC permission, then updates selected action entries under the task IPC lock with copied rights and behavior/flavor/privilege metadata. It requires the control-port object to exist, allowing setup before `ipc_active` during spawn. Per-action label checks can exclude updates. After unlocking it releases displaced rights and consumes the incoming right; invalid validation leaves registrations untouched. [task_set_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4143-L4223).
task_swap_exception_ports: Validates the replacement and MAC policy, then requires `ipc_active` under the task IPC lock. For selected actions it groups identical old port/behavior/flavor triples into output masks and installs copies of the new right. The loop stops when output-group capacity is reached, limiting later changes as well as results. Stored old references and the supplied replacement right are released after unlocking. [task_swap_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4366-L4470).
task_get_exception_ports_from_user: Requires conversion to a task-control object because it returns usable handler send rights. The internal query validates the mask and IPC activity, groups matching action triples under the task IPC lock, and copies one right per returned group up to capacity. Registrations remain unchanged. The wrapper releases its temporary task reference after both success and failure. [task_get_exception_ports_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4655-L4743). [Control-port wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4787-L4810).
task_get_exception_ports_info: Uses task-read conversion without evaluation and calls the same locked action enumerator in information-only mode. Instead of send rights, it returns hashed port and receiver-object identities, with zeros for invalid ports; matching actions are still merged into masks. This exposes handler metadata without granting the capability to message the handlers. The temporary task reference is released afterward. [task_get_exception_ports_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4655-L4784).
task_register_hardened_exception_handler: Requires an exception-compatible port and validates the allowed exception/behavior/flavor combination through the hardened path. It refuses an already-frozen task, sets the freeze flag, then takes the IPC lock and rejects a preexisting valid hardened handler. Success donates the incoming right into the task’s hardened action along with the signed-PC key and allowed masks; ordinary per-exception action arrays are not installed here. [task_register_hardened_exception_handler](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4842-L4898).
task_policy_set: Dispatches category, latency/throughput QoS and platform-specific suppression policy after validating layout and values. Control/graphics roles require privileged self requests, and embedded systems reject self category changes. Suppression updates requested-policy fields under the task lock, recomputes effective policy, then performs deferred completion outside the lock. A configured suppression-disable switch can return success without applying an active suppression request. [task_policy_set](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task_policy.c#L347-L529).
task_policy_get: Returns flavor-specific requested policy or defaults, with count checks before writing each layout. Category defaults are unspecified; QoS defaults use unspecified tiers, while actual values are repackaged from policy fields. The detailed TASK_POLICY_STATE flavor requires a privileged caller and locks the task to snapshot requested/effective and importance state. Unsupported flavors fail rather than returning a generic policy record. [task_policy_get](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task_policy.c#L575-L690).
task_get_state: This operates on the task’s default machine state inherited by subsequently created threads, not the live register state of every existing thread. It validates the task, holds its mutex across an activity check and the machine-task get/set callback, then returns that callback’s flavor/count result. An inactive task fails before the architecture callback. [task_get_state](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L7100-L7127).
task_set_state: This operates on the task’s default machine state inherited by subsequently created threads, not the live register state of every existing thread. It validates the task, holds its mutex across an activity check and the machine-task get/set callback, then returns that callback’s flavor/count result. An inactive task fails before the architecture callback. [task_set_state](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L7069-L7096).
task_set_phys_footprint_limit: With memorystatus enabled, requires footprint-management privilege and preserves the task’s existing active/fatal policy while changing the physical-footprint ledger limit. The helper reports the old limit, treats `-1` as the configured global maximum or infinity, and checks a current task’s new balance after an actual update. CONFIG_NOMONITORS bypasses ordinary new-limit enforcement; without CONFIG_MEMORYSTATUS the RPC is a failure stub. [task_set_phys_footprint_limit](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L7533-L7555). [Ledger updates](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L7600-L7716), [disabled configuration](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L7826-L7832).
task_purgable_info: Validates both the task and output pointer, takes an additional task reference around `vm_purgeable_stats`, and drops it before returning success. The helper supplies per-task purgeable-object statistics; this operation does not change purgeability or force a purge, despite sharing the purgeable-memory subsystem. [task_purgable_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L6917-L6931).
task_get_mach_voucher: For a non-null task, always returns a null voucher and success; the selector is unused. A null task returns `KERN_INVALID_TASK`. This compatibility body does not read the task’s bank context or synthesize a default voucher from it. [task_get_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L8822-L8833).
task_set_mach_voucher: Only validates that the task is non-null, then returns success while ignoring the supplied voucher. It does not store a voucher, update accounting attribution or alter thread vouchers. The separate thread-level setter contains the actual voucher/bank update mechanism. [task_set_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L8836-L8845).
task_swap_mach_voucher: Always returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`, but first releases the voucher reference in the in/out old-voucher argument because the generated MIG path does not release that reference itself. The task and replacement voucher are unused; no compare-and-swap or task state update occurs. [task_swap_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L8848-L8861).
task_generate_corpse: Rejects null/kernel targets and an existing corpse fork. It temporarily promotes the caller while the internal generator creates the corpse, then drops the returned thread reference, waits under the new task’s lock for thread termination, and resets eligible thread ports. Finally it transfers the corpse task reference into a control port with no-senders tracking, tying subsequent corpse lifetime to that capability. [task_generate_corpse](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L440-L490).
task_map_corpse_info: The 64-bit path requires a noncorpse destination and a corpse source with a valid kcdata buffer. It maps the fixed-size corpse-info allocation through `task_map_kcdata_64` and publishes address/size only after mapping succeeds. The older entry invokes that path and narrows successful address and size outputs to its legacy types; it does not create a second mapping implementation. [task_map_corpse_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L888-L950). The common mapper allocates in `task->map` but uses ordinary `copyout` and ignores its return value, so allocation success is not proof that copying the buffer succeeded. [Mapper body](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L855-L873).
task_map_corpse_info_64: The 64-bit path requires a noncorpse destination and a corpse source with a valid kcdata buffer. It maps the fixed-size corpse-info allocation through `task_map_kcdata_64` and publishes address/size only after mapping succeeds. The older entry invokes that path and narrows successful address and size outputs to its legacy types; it does not create a second mapping implementation. [task_map_corpse_info_64](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L888-L950). The common mapper allocates in `task->map` but uses ordinary `copyout` and ignores its return value, so allocation success is not proof that copying the buffer succeeded. [Mapper body](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L855-L873).
task_map_kcdata_object_64: Requires a noncorpse destination task and a valid kcdata object with a backing buffer. It maps the fixed backtrace-info allocation into the target through the common kcdata mapper using the BTINFO memory tag. Output address and size are written only after success; an absent buffer or invalid object fails without publishing a mapping result. [task_map_kcdata_object_64](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L962-L993). The common mapper allocates in `task->map` but uses ordinary `copyout` and ignores its return value, so allocation success is not proof that copying the buffer succeeded. [Mapper body](../../../xnu/osfmk/corpses/corpse.c#L855-L873).
task_register_dyld_image_infos: Emits dyld UUID map trace events through `kdebug_trace_dyld`; it does not maintain a queryable kernel image registry. If tracing is disabled, the helper discards the incoming VM copy and succeeds before checking task identity. Otherwise only the current task is accepted, the copy is mapped into the IPC kernel map, each image is traced, and the mapped input is deallocated afterward. [task_register_dyld_image_infos](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9055-L9109).
task_unregister_dyld_image_infos: Emits dyld UUID unmap trace events through `kdebug_trace_dyld`; it does not maintain a queryable kernel image registry. If tracing is disabled, the helper discards the incoming VM copy and succeeds before checking task identity. Otherwise only the current task is accepted, the copy is mapped into the IPC kernel map, each image is traced, and the mapped input is deallocated afterward. [task_unregister_dyld_image_infos](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9055-L9109).
task_get_dyld_image_infos: The body ignores its arguments and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. Registration RPCs nearby emit tracing events rather than populating an image list that this operation can retrieve. [task_get_dyld_image_infos](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9112-L9117).
task_register_dyld_shared_cache_image_in: Accepts only the current task, then emits one shared-cache UUID trace record. The no-cache and private-cache flags are explicitly unused. Success indicates acceptance by this tracing entry, not registration of a new VM shared region or validation of a cache mapping. [task_register_dyld_shared_cache_image_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9120-L9131).
task_register_dyld_set_dyld_state: The local body ignores the declared state arguments and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. It neither stores nor retrieves dyld process state; the retained MIG layout provides compatibility, not an active state service. [task_register_dyld_set_dyld_state](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9134-L9139).
task_register_dyld_get_process_state: The local body ignores the declared state arguments and returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`. It neither stores nor retrieves dyld process state; the retained MIG layout provides compatibility, not an active state service. [task_register_dyld_get_process_state](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9141-L9146).
task_inspect: When pervasive CPI accounting is enabled, accepts BASIC_COUNTS with a sufficiently large output and sums the task’s lifetime recount usage into instruction and cycle totals. It writes the resulting count only on success; unknown flavors fail. Without CONFIG_PERVASIVE_CPI the entire implementation returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`, independently of the declared inspection capability. [task_inspect](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9148-L9194).
task_get_exc_guard_behavior: Rejects a null task, otherwise returns its current `task_exc_guard` flags directly. The getter performs no mutation or policy relaxation and does not promise a mutex-protected multi-field snapshot; it reads this one behavior field. [task_get_exc_guard_behavior](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9464-L9473).
task_set_exc_guard_behavior: Rejects unknown flags, masks requested behavior to the configuration’s supported set, and updates the guard field. Release builds use an atomic compare/update loop that forbids changes covered by the no-unset/no-set masks while allowing corpse-bit changes; DEBUG/DEVELOPMENT builds assign the masked value directly. A disallowed downgrade/upgrade returns `KERN_DENIED` without installing that attempted value. [task_set_exc_guard_behavior](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9476-L9509).
mach_task_is_self: After rejecting a null converted task, compares object identity with `current_task()` and writes the boolean result. It does not compare PID values, task-port names or right counts; different capability flavors resolving to the same task therefore identify the same self task. [mach_task_is_self](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L1210-L1221).
task_dyld_process_info_notify_register: Validates a stashable live send right and MAC policy, obtains the target’s dyld info address, then serializes notifier-array changes with the global dyld mutex and task IPC lock. It clears dead entries, rejects duplicates, and inserts into a free slot or returns no-space. The helper updates userspace’s notification magic with copyout errors ignored and releases removed rights after unlocking; success consumes the new right. [task_dyld_process_info_notify_register](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L6512-L6626).
task_dyld_process_info_notify_deregister: Resolves a receive-right name in the caller’s space and temporarily references that port. Under the dyld global/task IPC locks it removes matching notifier rights and stale dead entries, then frees an empty array or refreshes the userspace magic through the shared helper. Removed send rights and the temporary port reference are released; absence of the requested registration returns failure. [task_dyld_process_info_notify_deregister](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L6651-L6735).
task_create_identity_token: Allocates a token, then validates the target under its task lock. A corpse is identified by task unique ID; a live BSD task uses an exact-process identity, while inactive or non-BSD ordinary tasks fail and free the allocation. The initialized token reference is intended for no-senders ownership, avoiding a permanently retained ordinary task reference merely to represent identity. [task_create_identity_token](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task_ident.c#L127-L162).
task_identity_token_get_task_port: Resolves the recorded exact process/corpse identity to a referenced task, so exit or identity mismatch can produce not-found. Corpses only support CONTROL conversion. Self CONTROL takes a fast path; other strong flavors undergo task-conversion policy, and foreign tasks also undergo MAC checks. Successful flavor conversion consumes the task reference; denial releases it without publishing a capability. [task_identity_token_get_task_port](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task_ident.c#L165-L264).
task_test_sync_upcall: Only DEBUG/DEVELOPMENT builds implement this test hook. It requires the current task and a valid send port, performs the synchronous kernel upcall, then releases the supplied send right and returns success. Other builds return `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; the test path is not a general arbitrary-target task callback facility. [task_test_sync_upcall](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L10224-L10242).
task_test_async_upcall_propagation: The development/debug hook validates self task, send port, QoS and IO-tier bounds before propagating attributes to the port. Attribute-propagation failure returns before the upcall. Success temporarily enables send importance for the current thread, makes the async upcall, disables importance again, and consumes the send right. Release builds return not-supported. [task_test_async_upcall_propagation](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L10246-L10287).
task_set_corpse_forking_behavior: In DEBUG/DEVELOPMENT builds, validates the task and updates TF_NO_CORPSE_FORKING under its lock according to the diagnostic-disable bit. Other bits are not separately rejected by this body. Production builds ignore the arguments and return `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; this is not a universal control over production corpse generation. [task_set_corpse_forking_behavior](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/task.c#L9512-L9534).
thread_create_from_user: Uses the user creation helper, which rejects kernel/null tasks and applies MAC checks to foreign-task creation. The new thread starts with one legacy user stop count and a corresponding hold, plus another hold if its task is suspended. Creation statistics are updated, then task/global thread-list locks are released before the thread reference is returned. The initial continuation is the user bootstrap-return path. [thread_create_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L1587-L1648).
thread_create_running_from_user: After target/MAC checks, creates a thread with the user bootstrap continuation, preserves any task-wide hold, and translates the supplied user register state before installing it. State conversion or installation failure unlocks the task/global lists, terminates the new thread, and drops its reference. Only successful state setup reaches `thread_start`; creation accounting and output publication follow. [thread_create_running_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L1736-L1800).
thread_terminate_from_user: Rejects pthread-managed threads before reaching general termination. The internal path marks an active thread inactive under its mutex, posts the abort/APC work, interrupts an existing wait or starts a never-started thread so it can terminate, and unpins its control port. A successful remote request waits for the target to stop; the target still performs final termination itself. [thread_terminate_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L285-L379).
thread_get_state_to_user: The helper holds the thread mutex and, for an active remote thread, places a hold, drops the mutex, and stops it before reading machine state. It un-stops and releases that hold afterward; interrupted stopping returns aborted. Inspection threads can still supply state after activity ends. A successful machine read is then translated to the user representation, including architecture-specific state authentication rules. [thread_get_state_to_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L832-L914).
act_get_state_to_user: This compatibility activation entry rejects the current thread, then calls `thread_get_state_to_user`. Consequently its remaining behavior is the same stop/hold/read/translate protocol used for remote thread state, including inspection-state support and aborted/terminated failures. It is not a separate saved-state object or alternative register representation. [act_get_state_to_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L1568-L1580).
thread_set_state_from_user: Requests entitlement-aware state conversion through the shared setter. Security policy is checked before taking the thread mutex and may arrange a guard violation; denied changes return no-access. User state is authenticated/translated before a remote thread is held and stopped, then the machine setter installs it. Every stop branch releases the hold, and external-modification statistics increment only after successful user-originated installation. [thread_set_state_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L922-L1018).
act_set_state_from_user: Rejects a request targeting the current thread and forwards all other arguments to the ordinary user-state setter. This preserves that setter’s security checks, authenticated conversion, stop/hold protocol and cleanup. The activation name therefore adds a self-target restriction rather than providing a bypass around thread_set_state policy. [act_set_state_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L1532-L1544).
thread_suspend: Under the thread mutex, increments both total and legacy user stop counts; only transition from zero total user holds adds the underlying thread hold. It rejects kernel-task threads and inactive targets, and waits for a remote target to stop after unlocking. The body does not create a resume-port right despite the broader historical comment above it. [thread_suspend](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L454-L476). [Public wait ordering](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L550-L571).
thread_resume: Requires a live nonkernel thread and a nonzero legacy stop count, then decrements legacy and total user counts under the thread mutex. Only the last user count releases the underlying hold. That release starts an unstarted thread or wakes a thread parked for suspension. A normal token-based suspension alone cannot satisfy the legacy-resume check. [thread_resume](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L430-L534). [Public wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L574-L587).
thread_suspend2: Preallocates a resume kobject port before locking, places a normal hold, and installs the port if necessary. It makes a send right while holding the thread mutex, so the make-send count serializes against no-senders cleanup. Unused preallocated ports are deallocated; remote targets are waited for after unlocking. The implementation returns a send right shared by normal suspensions, not a unique send-once right per call. [thread_suspend2](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L590-L652).
thread_resume2: Looks up the thread-resume kobject while holding the token port’s queue lock and acquires a thread reference before unlocking. Invalid/stale tokens fail. It releases a normal hold under the thread mutex, then drops the temporary thread reference. Port-right consumption is governed by the message declaration/IPC path, not an explicit release of the token port in this body. [thread_resume2](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L655-L683).
thread_abort: Locks the thread mutex, rejects an inactive thread, marks abort/APC state through `act_abort`, and tries to clear the current wait with `THREAD_INTERRUPTED`. The helper uses the scheduler lock at raised interrupt level, ends priority depression, and upgrades an already pending safe abort to an ordinary abort. This asks the target to unwind at kernel-defined points; it does not directly edit user registers. [thread_abort](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L721-L762).
thread_abort_safely: Under the thread mutex and scheduler lock, first tries to interrupt a wait only if the thread is at a safe point. Otherwise it records abort-safe state and posts APC work if no abort is already pending, also ending depression. Inactive threads return terminated; success can mean deferred abort processing rather than immediate removal from a wait queue. [thread_abort_safely](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L765-L798).
thread_depress_abort_from_user: Holds the thread mutex and rejects inactive targets. The helper additionally takes the scheduler lock at raised interrupt level, refuses to cancel poll-depression, and returns `KERN_NOT_DEPRESSED` when no ordinary depression is eligible. Otherwise it clears depression flags, recomputes scheduling priority and cancels the depression timer, decrementing its active count only when cancellation succeeds. [Wrapper](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L692-L712), [depression and timer handling](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/syscall_subr.c#L507-L556).
thread_get_special_port_from_user: Converts the destination to an inspectable thread, preserves its actual capability flavor, and applies the movable-self-control policy check for a thread of the current task. The selector allows a read capability to obtain read/inspect, while inspect permits inspect only. The internal helper checks activity under the thread mutex and copies/converts the selected capability; the wrapper drops its temporary thread reference. [thread_get_special_port_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L1515-L1678).
thread_set_special_port: Only THREAD_KERNEL_PORT is recognized. A permitted write requires CONFIG_CSR and a successful CSR kernel-debugger exception check; the configuration-disabled body returns KERN_NO_ACCESS as well. The body rejects un-stashable send rights and inactive targets; allowed writes store the supplied right under the thread mutex. Its local `old` variable remains null, so the apparent release block does not actually capture/release the prior settable-self right in this implementation. [thread_set_special_port](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L1700-L1755).
thread_info: Holds the thread mutex and admits either active or inspection threads, allowing corpse-style inspection after normal activity ends. Flavor-specific work takes the scheduler lock as needed: BASIC_INFO snapshots accounted state, IDENTIFIER_INFO returns thread ID/handle/dispatch address, and scheduler layouts validate the actual scheduling mode. FIFO_INFO is explicitly invalid-policy; count checks precede writing each supported layout. [thread_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L805-L829). [Flavor implementation](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L2036-L2185).
thread_set_exception_ports: Validates mask, port suitability, behavior and state flavor for a nonhardened update before applying MAC policy. Under the thread mutex it rejects inactive targets, lazily creates an exception-action array, and updates selected permitted entries with copied rights and metadata. Displaced rights and the incoming right are released after unlocking; per-action label policy can prevent individual changes. [thread_set_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4024-L4140).
thread_swap_exception_ports: After common validation/MAC checks, locks the thread, rejects inactivity, and lazily allocates its action array. It returns grouped old port/behavior/flavor triples while replacing selected actions with copied new rights. The loop stops when the supplied result capacity is reached, so later exceptions are not necessarily changed. Cleanup releases displaced references and the incoming right after unlocking. [thread_swap_exception_ports](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4253-L4362).
thread_get_exception_ports_from_user: Requires thread-control conversion to return actual handler rights. The shared query validates activity and mask under the thread mutex; an unallocated action array yields zero groups. Otherwise identical port/behavior/flavor triples share a mask, with copied send rights returned up to capacity. Stored registrations remain owned by the thread, and the wrapper drops its temporary thread reference. [thread_get_exception_ports_from_user](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4492-L4589). [Control conversion](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4632-L4653).
thread_get_exception_ports_info: Uses thread-read conversion without evaluation and selects information-only enumeration. The locked query groups actions as usual but fills hashed port/receiver identities instead of granting handler send rights; invalid ports produce zero identities. It preallocates FP state before locking to keep address hashing from allocating under thread locks, then returns the grouped count and releases the converted thread reference. [thread_get_exception_ports_info](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4492-L4629).
thread_adopt_exception_handler: Only a thread of the current task may adopt, and the task’s exception ports must already be frozen. It snapshots the registered hardened action under the task IPC lock, accepts only that handler port or null, and rejects masks not contained in the allowed exception/behavior/flavor masks. The ordinary internal thread updater then installs selected actions with the hardened flag, including its activity/MAC checks and right cleanup. [thread_adopt_exception_handler](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/ipc_tt.c#L4913-L4961).
thread_policy: Builds a historical policy-limit structure while holding the thread mutex. Without set_limit it rejects a base priority exceeding the thread’s current maximum; with set_limit it uses the supplied base as the proposed limit. It unlocks before calling `thread_set_policy`. The downstream implementation validates that limit but deliberately does not apply it, so this interface does not establish a new maximum priority. [thread_policy](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/mk_sp.c#L181-L355).
thread_set_policy: Accepts only the boot compatibility processor set and recognized timeshare/RR/FIFO layouts with exact base/limit counts and valid priorities. It validates the supplied maximum but deliberately passes only policy and base priority to `thread_set_mode_and_absolute_pri`. RR and FIFO both map to fixed scheduling internally; neither the historical max-priority field nor an RR quantum is installed by this wrapper. [thread_set_policy](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/mk_sp.c#L70-L170). [Mode mapping](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_policy.c#L631-L648).
thread_policy_set: Rejects forbidden static/QoS changes and work-interval configurations that disallow realtime. Existing QoS is temporarily removed and restored if applying the replacement fails. The internal dispatcher holds the thread mutex, validates flavor/count, and uses scheduler locking for mode/priority changes; realtime computation is raised toward half the constraint and capped. Affinity drops the mutex before taking task-level locks; deferred policy effects complete after unlocking. [thread_policy_set](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_policy.c#L265-L623).
thread_policy_get: Locks the thread and rejects inactivity, then reads flavor-specific policy or returns requested defaults. Scheduler fields are additionally protected by the scheduler lock; demoted threads can report their saved mode. Asking realtime policy of a non-realtime thread switches the result to defaults. Detailed policy-state inspection is privileged, affinity is architecture-dependent, and unsupported/count-invalid flavors return errors. [thread_policy_get](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_policy.c#L1283-L1494).
thread_get_mach_voucher: Ignores the selector and reads `ith_voucher` under the thread mutex. If a voucher exists it takes an additional reference before unlocking; otherwise it returns null with success. This is a snapshot reference, so a later voucher replacement does not invalidate the object returned to the caller. No active-thread check is performed in this body. [thread_get_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L3422-L3446).
thread_set_mach_voucher: Derives bank ledger, thread group and persona metadata before locking. Under the thread mutex it allows only the current thread or one not yet started, references the new voucher, replaces `ith_voucher`, and clears the cached voucher name. After unlocking it updates bank attribution/thread-group state and releases the old voucher. A started remote target fails before replacement. [thread_set_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L3460-L3509).
thread_swap_mach_voucher: The compare/swap operation is no longer supported. It still releases the in/out old-voucher reference to compensate for the generated MIG ownership convention, then returns `KERN_NOT_SUPPORTED`; neither thread state nor the supplied replacement is installed. [thread_swap_mach_voucher](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread.c#L3521-L3534).
thread_convert_thread_state: Validates direction and output capacity, then chooses source/destination authentication contexts between the named thread and current thread. It converts input from the source’s user representation to kernel form and then into the destination’s user representation while preserving flags. Only successful conversion with adequate final capacity copies the result out. This transforms a supplied state blob; it does not install registers into either thread. [thread_convert_thread_state](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L1021-L1083).
thread_raise_exception: The Rosetta implementation requires a thread in the current translated task and rejects EXC_CRASH. It constructs the code pair and delivers through host exception actions using the host lock; failure propagates without resuming. On successful delivery it calls ordinary `thread_resume`, so that final resume can itself fail if no eligible legacy suspension exists. [thread_raise_exception](../../../xnu/osfmk/kern/thread_act.c#L1443-L1480).
